a1.cap: Can You Hop to the End?
a1.say: Let's solve Can You Hop to the End?, using the Greedy Reach approach.

card.title: Can You Hop to the End?

a1.cap: You start at index 0. nums[i] is the farthest jump length from index i. Return true if you can reach the last index.
a1.say: You start at index 0. nums at i is the farthest jump length from index i. Return true if you can reach the last index.

lines: You start at index 0. nums[i] is the farthest jump length from index i. Return true if you can reach the last index.

a1.cap: For example, with nums = [2,3,1,1,4], the answer is true.
a1.say: For example, with nums equals 2, 3, 1, 1, 4, the answer is true.

a1.cap: Walk left to right keeping reach, the farthest index you can get to. If you ever stand on an index beyond reach, you're stuck. Otherwise extend reach with i + nums[i].
a1.say: Walk left to right keeping reach, the farthest index you can get to. If you ever stand on an index beyond reach, you're stuck. Otherwise extend reach with i plus nums at i.

a1.cap: Let's walk through it with nums = [2,3,1,1,4].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with nums equals 2, 3, 1, 1, 4.

a1.cap: From index 0 you can jump to 2. Farthest so far: 2.
From index 1 you can jump to 4. Farthest so far: 4.
From index 2 you can jump to 3. Farthest so far: 4.
From index 3 you can jump to 4. Farthest so far: 4.
From index 4 you can jump to 8. Farthest so far: 8.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Greedy Reach approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
